hints.title: Use total distance divided by total time
hints.body: For each proposed journey, calculate V=d1+d2t1+t2. Since the two speeds are 50 and 40, the claimed mean is 45 in every case. A counterexample needs an actual overall speed different from 45.
hints.recap: The average speed of a complete journey is its total distance divided by its total duration.
hints.pitfall: Weight the two speeds by their durations before deciding whether the unweighted mean applies.
hints.pause: Find the missing times in I and III, and the missing distances in II.

recall.reminder: Recover the component totals and combine them with the correct weights.

hints.title: Find each duration
hints.body: For the journeys specified by distance, divide each leg’s distance by its own speed. For the journey specified by time, multiply speed by time to obtain each distance.
hints.recap: Each leg contributes its own time and distance.
hints.pitfall: Equal distances do not imply equal durations.
hints.pause: Construct the totals for all three journeys.

recall.reminder: Each leg contributes its own time and distance.

hints.title: Compare exactly with the claimed mean
hints.body: For each journey form total distance divided by total time. Cross-multiply to compare each exact fraction with the claimed arithmetic mean.
hints.recap: A counterexample meets the setup and makes its conclusion false.
hints.pitfall: A journey agreeing with the claim is a supporting example.
hints.pause: Classify all three journeys and select precisely the counterexamples.

recall.reminder: A counterexample meets the setup and makes its conclusion false.

solution:
1. Identify the claimed result. In each journey, 12(u+v)=12(50+40)=45.

2. Calculate the actual overall speeds. In I, V=100+100100/50+100/40=2009/2=4009≠45. In II, V=50+401+1=45. In III, V=80+10080/50+100/40=18041/10=180041≠45.

3. Select the counterexamples. I and III make the claimed conclusion false, whereas II agrees with it.

Answer F. For different speeds, equal time weights justify the simple mean; the other journeys need the full distance-over-time calculation.
knowledgePattern: Test claimed arithmetic-mean speed against weighted journey examples
